# Planetary Gearbox — OpenSCAD Design

A fully parametric compound planetary gearbox designed in OpenSCAD.
All geometry is driven by a single source file: `planetary.gearbox.scad`.

---

## File Structure

```
planetary.gearbox.scad      ← single source of truth, all modules and parameters
extract_parts.sh            ← splits source into per-part .scad files
build_all.sh                ← renders all parts to STL headlessly (no GUI)
README.md                   ← this file
```

### Per-part SCAD files (generated by extract_parts.sh)

| File | Part |
|---|---|
| `sun_gear.scad` | Sun gear with shaft bore and D-cut flat |
| `planet_gear.scad` | Planet gears with bearing pockets |
| `ring_gear.scad` | Ring gear / gearbox body |
| `carrier_top.scad` | Top carrier plate with output shaft hub |
| `carrier_bottom.scad` | Bottom carrier plate |
| `housing_bottom.scad` | Bottom housing plate |
| `housing_top.scad` | Top housing plate |
| `housing_wall.scad` | Housing side wall |
| `bearing_shaft_spacer.scad` | Bearing shaft spacers |

---

## Dependencies

The following OpenSCAD libraries must be installed before opening or rendering:

- **BOSL2** — https://github.com/revarbat/BOSL2
  Install to: `~/.local/share/OpenSCAD/libraries/BOSL2/`
- **Involute Gears** (`publicDomainGearV1.3_trinarylogic.scad`)
  — https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:2854963
  Install to: `~/.local/share/OpenSCAD/libraries/`

---

## Main Parameters

All parameters are defined at the top of `planetary.gearbox.scad`.

### Gear Configuration

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `teeth_sun` | Number of teeth on the sun gear |
| `teeth_planet` | Number of teeth on each planet gear |
| `teeth_ring` | Number of teeth on the ring gear |
| `gear_module` | Gear module (tooth size) in mm — larger = bigger teeth |
| `gear_thickness` | Face width / height of all gears in mm |
| `gear_pressure_angle` | Pressure angle in degrees (typically 20°) |
| `gear_mesh_clearance` | Backlash / clearance between meshing gears in mm |

> **Valid gear ratio check:** `teeth_ring = teeth_sun + 2 × teeth_planet`
> Gear ratio = `1 + (teeth_ring / teeth_sun)`

### Carrier

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `carrier_plate_diameter` | Outer diameter of carrier top and bottom plates |
| `carrier_plate_thickness` | Thickness of each carrier plate |
| `carrier_spacing` | Distance between top and bottom carrier plates (pillar length) |
| `carrier_total_height` | Total assembled height of the carrier |
| `calculated_carrier_radius` | Computed radius to planet gear centres |
| `planet_angles_list` | List of 3 angles (degrees) where planet gears are positioned |
| `carrier_to_planets_clearance` | Radial clearance between planet outer edge and carrier wall |

### Output Shaft

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `shaft_diameter_output` | Output shaft bore diameter |
| `hub_diameter_output` | Outer diameter of the output hub cylinder |
| `hub_height_output` | Height of the output hub cylinder |
| `tolerance_output_bore` | Fit tolerance added to shaft bore |
| `setscrew_output_diameter` | Set screw diameter for shaft locking |

### Bearings

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `bearing_683_id` | Inner diameter of planet bearings (683 series) |
| `bearing_683_od` | Outer diameter of planet bearings |
| `planet_bearing_pocket_depth` | Depth of bearing pocket in planet gear |

### Housing

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `housing_size` | Overall square footprint of the housing in mm |
| `wall_thickness` | Housing wall thickness in mm |
| `housing_wall_height_clearance` | Extra height added to housing wall above carrier |
| `box_chamfer_size` | Chamfer size on housing corners |

### Tolerances

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `tolerance_shaft` | General shaft fit tolerance in mm |
| `tolerance_output_bore` | Output shaft bore tolerance in mm |

## Switching Parts On/Off

Near the top of the instantiation section in `planetary.gearbox.scad` there is a
block of boolean render switches:

```openscad
// ============================================================================
// PART RENDER SWITCHES — set only one to true per file
// ============================================================================
render_sun_gear       = false;
render_planet_gear    = false;
render_carrier_top    = false;
render_carrier_bottom = false;
render_ring_gear      = false;
render_housing_bottom = false;
render_housing_top    = false;
render_housing_wall   = false;
render_bearing_shaft  = false;
```

Set exactly **one** to `true` to preview or render that part in the OpenSCAD GUI.
All others remain `false` so only the selected part is shown.

Example — to preview the carrier top:
```openscad
render_carrier_top = true;
```

---

## Rendering to STL

### Single part (GUI)

Open `planetary.gearbox.scad` in OpenSCAD, set the desired render switch to `true`,
then press **F6** to render and **File → Export → Export as STL**.

### Single part (command line, no GUI)

```bash
openscad -o carrier_top.stl planetary.gearbox.scad -D "render_carrier_top=true"
```

The `-D` flag overrides a variable at render time without modifying the source file.

### All parts at once

```bash
chmod +x build_all.sh
./build_all.sh planetary.gearbox.scad

# Or into a specific output folder
./build_all.sh planetary.gearbox.scad ./stl
```

This calls OpenSCAD once per part in headless mode, producing one STL per part.

---

## Splitting into Per-Part SCAD Files

If you want separate `.scad` files for each part (useful for editing a single part
in the GUI without the full assembly loading):

```bash
chmod +x extract_parts.sh
./extract_parts.sh planetary.gearbox.scad
```

Each output file is an exact copy of the source with:
- The corresponding `render_X` switch set to `true`
- All `z_offset_*` variables set to `0` so the part sits at the origin

---

## Assembly Order

```
1. Housing bottom plate
2. Ring gear body (press-fit or screw into housing)
3. Carrier bottom plate
4. Planet gears (on carrier bottom axle screws, with bearings)
5. Sun gear (driven by motor shaft)
6. Carrier top plate (secured with M3 screws + captured hex nuts)
7. Housing wall
8. Housing top plate
```

### Carrier Fasteners

The carrier top plate has **6 M3 holes** evenly spaced at 60° intervals:
- 3 holes align with the **planet axle screws** (M3 screws act as planet shafts)
- 3 holes align with the **carrier pillars** (connect top and bottom plates)

Every hole has a **hex nut pocket** recessed into the top face of the plate,
extending up into the hub cylinder so nuts can be slid in horizontally before
the assembly is closed. Screws are driven from below.

---

## Known Issues / Notes

- Preview resolution is set via `$fn` — lower for faster preview, higher for final render
- Gear backlash / mesh clearance may need tuning depending on printer tolerance
- Planet gear count is fixed at 3; changing this requires updating `planet_angles_list`
- The ring gear and housing body are combined in a single module (`ring_gear_box_body`)
